Each release candidate of SCGSim 3.0 changed some calls, with no compatibility
layer: a script written for an earlier version stops with an error that names
the call to change. Find the version your code was written for, then work
through its checklist. Each checklist goes straight to the current version
and shows the final code. Until you are ready, keep the version your study project pins;
nothing changes for it.

## Find your version {#find-your-version}

The version is the tag your project installs (`@v3.0.0rc3` in its
`pyproject.toml`), or what
`python -c 'from importlib.metadata import version; print(version("scgsim"))'`
prints.

| Your code was written for | What changes most | Your checklist |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0.0rc5 or 3.0.0rc6 | Nothing in your code. Prepare your models again, run Palace Route A again, and save Palace EPR results again | [From 3.0.0rc5 or rc6](#from-3-0-0rc6) |
| 3.0.0rc4 | Junctions, lumped RLCs and Driven ports are declared on the plan, not on the simulation | [From 3.0.0rc4](#from-3-0-0rc4) |
| 3.0.0rc3 | Surface EPR and the vacuum region are set on the plan, not on the simulation | [From 3.0.0rc3](#from-3-0-0rc3) |
| 3.0.0rc1 or 3.0.0rc2 | The layout check takes the plan, and AEDT builds every 3D model from the plan | [From 3.0.0rc1 or rc2](#from-rc1-or-rc2) |
| 2.0 (a 2.0.0 release candidate) | Palace builds its model with SGB and has new mesh controls; the route and Surface EPR are two settings; old run folders are not read | [From 2.0](#from-2-0) |

Code older than 2.0, which imports `scgsim.sgb`, first moves its imports with
the [old-import inventory](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#geometry-api),
then follows From 2.0.

## From 3.0.0rc5 or rc6 {#from-3-0-0rc6}

Nothing in your code changes. From 3.0.0rc6 on, an install without the `aedt`
extra imports `scgsim.aedt` and `scgsim.visualization`. Three changes affect
what you prepared, ran or saved:

- **Prepare it again.** An SGB model now says it is `scgsim.sgb.sidecar.v7`.
  A model, Palace run folder or AEDT handoff prepared with 3.0.0rc6 or earlier
  is refused wherever SCGSim reads its model, with an error that says to
  rebuild it. An older Route A model does not state the edges of its films,
  which the mesh is now sized from. Call `plan.prepare()` and prepare the
  simulation again.
- **Run Palace Route A again.** On Route A (`set_route("A")`), 3.0.0rc6 and
  earlier meshed the edge of each film at the model's coarse size, so a CPW
  gap could be a single element across. The results came out far off, with no
  error: on a CPW test layout, sizing the edges moved the first Eigenmode
  frequency from 2.04 to 4.12 GHz and the capacitance from 1.19 to 0.29 pF.
  Each film's edge is now meshed as on Route B, so a Route A mesh has about
  as many unknowns as Route B's.
  Route B and AEDT are not affected.
- **Save Palace EPR results again.** Each Eigenmode EPR row now has an
  `external` group, the coupling loss of each port with a resistance, and an
  Eigenmode run whose ports are all resistive, such as 50 Ω feedline ports, is
  read instead of refused. A detached EPR result saved with 3.0.0rc6 or
  earlier (`scgsim.palace.epr-result.v2`) has no such group, so
  `resolve_epr_result` refuses it; save `epr_result()` of the new run again
  ([What a result holds](../reference/specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#results-and-offline-analysis)).

## From 3.0.0rc4 {#from-3-0-0rc4}

[]{#lumped-elements-on-the-plan}A lumped element (a junction, a resistor, a
capacitor, or the port a measurement drives) is a fact of the device, the same
for every solver, so it is now declared once, on the `GeometryPlan`, by the
name of the port sheet it sits on. Palace and AEDT read it from the snapshot;
no simulation declares one of its own. Declared the old way or the new way, a
study builds the same model, byte for byte (the mesh, the Palace configuration
and the AEDT model files, checked on the roster's Eigenmode layouts and the
HFSS EPR acceptance case). Four other changes are at the end
of this section: [what you prepared with 3.0.0rc4](#models-from-rc4).

1. Replace Palace `sim.add_port(name, layer=..., layout_sheet=True, inductance=L)`
   with `LumpedElement(name, inductance_h=L)` in `plan.set_lumped_elements([...])`,
   before `plan.prepare()`. `layer` goes: the plan knows the sheet's layer. The
   elements keep the order you give them, so the first is still Palace's `P1`.
2. Replace AEDT `sim.add_junction(planar_junction_from_port(...))` and the
   `RectangularJunctionSpec` you gave `plan.set_rectangular_junctions(...)` with
   one `LumpedElement(sheet, inductance_h=L, capacitance_f=C)` on the plan. The
   plan finds the sheet's two conductors and their Nets itself. The junction's
   id is now its sheet's name: write that name in
   `EprAnalysisRequest(junction_ids=...)` and read it in the results.
3. Replace AEDT `sim.add_lumped_rlc(LumpedRlc(port_sheet_id, "parallel", ...))`
   with `LumpedElement(sheet, resistance_ohm=..., inductance_h=..., capacitance_f=...)`,
   named by the sheet's name, not its `port_sheet_id`. The components are in
   parallel, as in Palace; a series RLC is no longer declarable.
4. For HFSS Driven Terminal, replace the two `LumpedTerminalPort(...)` records,
   `prepare_sgb_model(..., ports=...)` and `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(model=..., ...)`
   with two `LumpedPort(sheet, reference_net=..., impedance_ohm=...)` on the plan
   and `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(plan.prepare(), modeling=..., ...)`.
   Port 1 is the first `LumpedPort` you give.
5. `simulation_drc` checks the plan's elements as the simulation builds them;
   it no longer gives every sheet a fixed 1 nH. A sheet the plan declares
   nothing on is left out of a Palace or HFSS model; before, HFSS refused it.

The code becomes:

```python
# Before
plan.set_rectangular_junctions([RectangularJunctionSpec("jj", ...)])
snapshot = plan.prepare()
sim = palace.EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.add_port("chip/J1", layer="metal", layout_sheet=True, inductance=10e-9)
hsim = aedt.EigenmodeSim(modeling="solid", aedt_version="2024.2")
hsim.set_plan(snapshot)
hsim.add_junction(planar_junction_from_port(snapshot.geometry_input, port_name="chip/J1",
                  junction_id="jj", terminal_a_net="A", terminal_b_net="B",
                  inductance_h=10e-9, capacitance_f=0.0))
hsim.set_epr_request(EprAnalysisRequest(junction_ids=("jj",)))

# Now
plan.set_lumped_elements([LumpedElement("chip/J1", inductance_h=10e-9)])
snapshot = plan.prepare()
sim = palace.EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
hsim = aedt.EigenmodeSim(modeling="solid", aedt_version="2024.2")
hsim.set_plan(snapshot)
hsim.set_epr_request(EprAnalysisRequest(junction_ids=("chip/J1",)))
```

| Removed | Now |
|---|---|
| Palace `EigenmodeSim.add_port`, `EigenmodeSim.ports` | `plan.set_lumped_elements([LumpedElement(...)])`; `sim.input_summary().data["backend"]["lumped_elements"]` |
| AEDT `EigenmodeSim.add_junction`, `add_lumped_rlc`, and the `junctions` and `lumped_rlcs` arguments | `LumpedElement` on the plan |
| `GeometryPlan.set_rectangular_junctions` | `LumpedElement` on the plan; the plan binds the sheet to its two conductors |
| `scgsim.aedt.LumpedTerminalPort`, `LumpedRlc`, `PlanarJunction`, `planar_junction_from_port`, `prepare_sgb_model`; `scgsim.aedt.specs.LumpedRlc`, `LumpedTerminalPort` | `LumpedElement` and `LumpedPort` from `scgsim.geometry`; HFSS builds its records from them |
| `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(model=...)` | `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(snapshot, modeling=..., ...)` |

Errors now come from `prepare()`, naming the element, its sheet's layer and its
place in µm: a sheet the layout does not draw, a sheet that lands on other than
two conductors, two conductors of one Net, or a port whose `reference_net` is
neither conductor's Net. [Lumped elements](../reference/specs/geometry-plan.qmd#lumped-elements)
gives the records, and [Supported calculations](../reference/supported-calculations.qmd#lumped-elements)
what each calculation does with them.

[]{#models-from-rc4}Four other changes affect what you prepared or ran with
3.0.0rc4:

- **Prepare it again.** An SGB model now says it is `scgsim.sgb.sidecar.v7`.
  A model, Palace run folder or AEDT handoff prepared with 3.0.0rc6 or earlier
  is refused wherever SCGSim reads its model, with an error that says to
  rebuild it. The old model may list a port sheet's two conductors in the
  other order, and read now it would put an HFSS Terminal on the wrong edge.
  Call `plan.prepare()` and prepare the simulation again.
- **Run HFSS Driven Terminal again** where the layout declares a port's
  signal conductor before its ground, as the OrcaPen SC PDK launcher does.
  3.0.0rc4 put the Terminal on the port sheet's ground edge; it is now on its
  signal edge.
- **Run HFSS Eigenmode again where a lumped element has a capacitance.**
  3.0.0rc4 and earlier wrote the capacitance in a unit AEDT reads as
  femtofarads, so the model held 10⁻¹⁵ times the capacitance you declared, with
  no error. This affects a Lumped RLC and an EPR junction given
  `capacitance_f`; their inductance and resistance were right, and Palace is
  not affected.
- **Run Palace Route A again**, as [From 3.0.0rc5 or rc6](#from-3-0-0rc6)
  explains.

## From 3.0.0rc3 {#from-3-0-0rc3}

[]{#plan-owns-surface-epr}Surface EPR and the vacuum region change the geometry
and do not depend on the solver, so from 3.0.0rc4 they are set once, on the
`GeometryPlan`. Run folders written by 3.0.0rc3 are read as before: the model,
the Palace configuration and the results are unchanged.

1. Replace `sim.set_surface_epr(specs)` with `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)`,
   before `plan.prepare()`, for Palace `EigenmodeSim` and `ElectrostaticSim`
   and AEDT `EigenmodeSim`. `None` turns it off and `{}` is refused, as before.
2. Replace the Palace `sim.set_vacuum_region(padding)` with
   `plan.set_vacuum_region(padding)`, before `plan.prepare()`.
3. Remove `surface_epr_specs=` from `simulation_drc(...)` on all three classes:
   the check reads the plan's. `route`, `approximation_profile` and `modeling`
   stay.
4. Remove the `surface_epr_specs` and `vacuum_region` arguments of the Palace
   simulation constructors, and `surface_epr_specs` of AEDT `EigenmodeSim`.
   `sim.surface_epr_specs` now reads the specs of the bound plan.
5. For AEDT `EigenmodeSim`, replace `set_geometry(...)`, `set_stack(...)` and the
   `component`, `build_input` and `stack` arguments with
   `sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())`, its only source.

The code becomes:

```python
# Before
sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_route("A")
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
sim.set_vacuum_region((0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
sim.set_surface_epr(specs)
EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, surface_epr_specs=specs, route="A")

# Now
plan.set_vacuum_region((0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
plan.set_surface_epr(specs)
EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, route="A")
sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_route("A")
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
```

The route is unchanged by this step: the check builds its own temporary
simulation, so its `route=` must be the one the simulation sets with
`set_route` (a simulation without `set_route` is Route B, and so is a check
without `route=`). The specs are checked by the same rules, against the plan's materials, when
you set them and again in `prepare()`. A refusal that named `set_surface_epr`
on the simulation now names `GeometryPlan.set_surface_epr`. HFSS Driven
Terminal and Q3D still read no Surface EPR and cut no bands.

Then declare the lumped elements on the plan: [From 3.0.0rc4](#from-3-0-0rc4).

## From 3.0.0rc1 or rc2 {#from-rc1-or-rc2}

Work through these steps in order.

1. **Old run folders.** Palace run folders written by 3.0.0rc1 are not read:
   from 3.0.0rc2 the returned record states how the solver ended, and result
   reading refuses one without it. HFSS and Q3D run folders written by
   3.0.0rc1 or rc2 came from AEDT's own geometry builder, which is gone: the AEDT runner,
   `resolve_results()` and `analyze_epr()` refuse them. Prepare and run such a
   study again, or read the old folder with the version that wrote it.
2. []{#simulation-drc-migration}**The layout check takes the plan.** The first
   argument of `simulation_drc` is the `GeometryPlan` the simulation will be
   given, before `prepare()`; `layer_stack`, `material_records`, `instances`,
   `nets` and `surface_epr_specs` are gone, because they are the plan's.

   ```python
   # Before
   EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(component, layer_stack=layer_stack, material_records=material_records, nets=nets, route="A")

   # Now
   plan = GeometryPlan(component=component, root_id="chip", layer_stack=layer_stack, material_records=material_records, coupon_padding_um=0.0)
   plan.set_nets(nets)
   plan.set_vacuum_region((0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
   plan.set_lumped_elements(elements)  # the junctions, loads and ports, when the device has any
   plan.set_surface_epr(specs)  # when the simulations compute Surface EPR
   EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, route="A")
   ```

   The check adds nothing to the plan. Before, it used zero coupon padding and,
   when the layout had no vacuum, a vacuum padded by (0, 0, 1000) µm; now it
   uses the plan's, and a plan without a vacuum region is refused. Register an
   assembly's instances with `plan.register_instance` before `set_nets`.
   [Check a layout](check-a-layout.qmd) shows the check and its report.
3. **Surface EPR, the vacuum region and the lumped elements on the plan.**
   Steps 1 to 5 of [From 3.0.0rc3](#from-3-0-0rc3), then
   [From 3.0.0rc4](#from-3-0-0rc4).
4. []{#aedt-sgb-migration}**AEDT builds from the plan.** Every 3D AEDT
   calculation is prepared from a `GeometryPlan` snapshot: AEDT imports the
   same model Palace meshes and builds no geometry of its own.

   | Calculation | Removed | Now |
   |---|---|---|
   | HFSS Eigenmode | `HfssEigenmodeSpec`, `gds_path` | `EigenmodeSim(modeling=..., aedt_version=...)`, `sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())`, `sim.prepare_handoff()`; see [HFSS Eigenmode](modes-hfss.qmd) |
   | HFSS Driven Terminal | `HfssDrivenSpec`, `HfssDrivenMode`, `LayerImport`, `ObjectBinding`, `LengthMeshSpec`, `PreparedPlanarGeometry`, `prepare_planar_geometry_input`; the `modeling`, `geometry`, `ports` and `geometry_workers` arguments of `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry` | two `LumpedPort`s on the plan, then `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(plan.prepare(), modeling=..., ...)`; see [HFSS Driven Terminal](s-parameters-hfss.qmd) |
   | Q3D | `Q3dBodySpec`; the `materials` and `region_padding_um` arguments of `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` | `prepare_q3d_from_geometry(snapshot, ...)`, with the stack's materials; see [Q3D](capacitance-q3d.qmd) |

   The rest of this step:

   - The AEDT Region is the plan's vacuum region, for every calculation;
     `region_padding_um` is gone.
   - The AEDT request's own physical layers (`PhysicalLayerSpec`) are gone:
     the plan's layer stack declares them, as `PhysicalLayerDeclaration`.
   - Surface EPR for HFSS Eigenmode is the plan's: `SurfaceEprSpec`,
     `combine_epr_mode` and `combine_surface_epr_mode` are gone.
     `EprAnalysisRequest.surface_contribution_ids` is now `surface_epr_groups`,
     and `analyze_epr(geometry=..., geometry_workers=...)` is now
     `analyze_epr(model=...)`.
   - `prepare_handoff(spec=...)` takes only `Q3dSpec` and `Q2dSpec`; an HFSS
     request is refused with the name of the HFSS function to call.
     `--geometry-workers` and `ExecutionOptions.geometry_workers` are gone.
   - Driven Modal and wave ports are not available. A two-port network is
     Driven Terminal with two `LumpedPort`s on the plan's port sheets
     ([issue #135](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/135) tracks
     Driven Modal).
   - Q3D extracts capacitance and conductance only: `Q3dTerminalPair`,
     `terminal_pairs`, `Q3dSpec.solve_ac_rl` and the `source_object`,
     `source_side`, `sink_object` and `sink_side` fields of `Q3dNetSpec` are
     gone ([issue #265](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/265)
     tracks AC/RL).
   - `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry` and `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` now
     refuse a model the AEDT import cannot realize before they write the
     handoff, without AEDT.
5. []{#palace-convergence-migration}**Convergence and reports** (new in
   3.0.0rc2; from rc2, skip this step). You can now
   [declare when a run has converged](convergence-and-reports.qmd#declare-convergence)
   with `sim.set_convergence(...)`; Palace is then stopped at that pass. With a
   declaration, a stated `amr_tolerance` is refused. The reports changed for
   every run, declared or not:

   ::: {.askr-table-compact}
   | Before | Now |
   |---|---|
   | Run Identity showed every recorded field | Problem, Route, Profile, AMR passes recorded and MPI × OpenMP; the rest with `show_details=True` |
   | `|Δ …| vs AMR pass` figures | Removed. With a declaration each quantity is followed by its declared change in percent |
   | One surface figure with MA, MS and SA | One figure per interface kind, a line for the whole surfaces and one per inset |
   | `show_physics_quantities()` opened with the surface ranking | It opens with the capacitance matrix, or each mode's frequency and Q |
   | `show_all_results()`: trust, benchmark, physics | Trust, physics, benchmark |
   | `show_simulation_benchmark()` took no `theme` | Every view takes `theme="light"` or `"dark"` |
   | A capacitance figure named `C[1][1]` | Named by its terminals, `C[signal][signal]` |
   :::

   `ResolvedPalaceResult.convergence` holds the check of every pass and the
   verdict, and `ResolvedPalaceResult.solver_end` how Palace ended.

## From 2.0 {#from-2-0}

Work through these steps in order, then continue with
[From 3.0.0rc1 or rc2](#from-rc1-or-rc2) from its step 2.

1. **Old run folders.** Palace now writes mesh manifest `schema_version` 2 and
   index map `schema_version` 3 and reads only those; run folders written by
   2.0 and detached EPR results of `scgsim.palace.epr-result.v1` are refused
   ([which ones](../reference/specs/report-model.qmd#palace-run-schemas)).
   AEDT results recorded before runtime-source schema
   `scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v30` are refused too. Prepare and run again, or
   read an old result with the version that wrote it.
2. **Imports.** Import every public name from its package: `scgsim.geometry`,
   `scgsim.palace`, `scgsim.aedt` or `scgsim.visualization`. The modules below
   them moved in 3.0 and keep no alias: for example
   `scgsim.palace.preparation.eigenmode` is gone, and
   `from scgsim.palace import EigenmodeSim` is the import to use.
   [The API index](../reference/api-index.qmd) lists the public names.
3. []{#palace-mesh-migration}[]{#geometry}**Palace builds its model with SGB.**
   `mesh()` builds the geometry with SGB and meshes it with `scgsim.meshing`.
   []{#mesh-controls}`set_mesh` takes new controls, alike on both Palace
   simulations
   ([Palace mesh controls](../reference/specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls)):

   ::: {.askr-table-compact}
   | Removed | Replacement |
   |---|---|
   | `size_policy`, `refined_mesh_size`, `max_mesh_size`; `set_numerical(refined_mesh_size=, max_mesh_size=)` | `recipe`: `FeatureRecipe` (default), `GlobalSizeRecipe` or `UniformBoundaryRecipe` |
   | `algorithm_3d` | `mesher=MesherOptions(algorithm_3d=...)`, with `scgsim.meshing.DELAUNAY` or `HXT` |
   | `geometry_order`, `high_order_optimize` | `MesherOptions(geometry_order=..., high_order_optimize=...)` |
   | `threads`, `surface_threads` | None: meshing runs on one thread, because HXT with several threads was not reproducible |
   | None | `quality_threshold` (default 0.01 minSICN) and `budgets` (`Budgets`) |
   :::

   No recipe reproduces an old mesh element for element. The closest to each
   former sizing choice:

   ::: {.askr-table-compact}
   | Former setting | Closest recipe | What changes |
   |---|---|---|
   | `scgsim_default` (refined 5 µm, maximum 300 µm) | `UniformBoundaryRecipe()` | Before, only the boundary, PEC and port curves were sized. Now every curve is sized; pass `MesherOptions(algorithm_2d=5)` to keep the old 2D algorithm. |
   | `gmsh_default` (no size field) | `GlobalSizeRecipe()` | The maximum size is now the bounding-box diagonal over 20, and the mesher is Delaunay by default. |
   | `algorithm_3d`, `threads` | `MesherOptions(algorithm_3d=...)` | Meshing runs on one thread. |
   :::

   The default is none of these: `FeatureRecipe()` sizes the curves the
   geometry calls for. With every recipe, a mesh that cannot reach the quality
   threshold now stops `mesh()` with `MeshRepairError`; before, mesh quality
   never stopped a run.
4. []{#surface-epr}**The route and Surface EPR are two settings.**
   `set_surface_epr(*, representation, specs, route_a_thin_film=None,
   approximation_profile=None)` on the simulation became
   `sim.set_route(route, *, approximation_profile=None)` and
   `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)`:

   ```python
   # Before
   sim.set_surface_epr(representation="A", specs=specs)

   # Now
   plan.set_surface_epr(specs)  # before plan.prepare()
   sim.set_route("A")
   ```

   - Route B is the default, so a Route B simulation calls `set_route` not at
     all. Route A is `set_route("A")`, with the `thin_film` profile;
     `substrate_face` and `metal_gap_equivalent` are
     `set_route("A", approximation_profile=profile)`. The keywords
     `representation` and `route_a_thin_film` are gone, and so are the
     simulation's `thin_film` field and the `thin_film` key of
     `input_summary()`, which now shows the profile's name.
   - Surface EPR is computed only when the plan was given specs, for
     Eigenmode and Electrostatic alike. Drop a call that asked for none (Route
     B with empty `specs`): an empty mapping is refused.
   - `inset_margins_um` takes only positive, strictly increasing margins, so
     drop a leading `0.0`: the row of the whole surface is always there.
   - Palace no longer writes native `Mask` or `Inset`, so margin rows need no
     special Palace build, and result reading refuses a config that has native
     `Mask` rows.
   - `inset_margins_by_entity_um` is new, for margins per conductor on `MA` and
     `MS`. `face_kinds` takes `sheet`, `top`, `bottom` and `interface`, and
     refuses `sidewall` when the spec asks for margins.

   The [Eigenmode contract](../reference/specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins)
   defines the keys and the names of the rows, such as `MA::pad__top::band=1`.
5. []{#results}**Renamed result records.** The new names have no alias:

   ::: {.askr-table-compact}
   | Before | Now |
   |---|---|
   | `SurfaceMaskEprRecord`, `SurfaceMaskEprSeriesSnapshot` | `SurfaceMarginEprRecord`, `SurfaceMarginEprSeriesSnapshot` |
   | `PhysicsQuantitiesReport.masked_snapshots` | `PhysicsQuantitiesReport.margin_snapshots` |
   | `scgsim.palace.epr-result.v1` | `scgsim.palace.epr-result.v3` |
   | `surface-mask-Q.csv` and `surface-mask-energy.csv` | Margin rows are read from `surface-Q.csv` |
   :::

## For contributors {#for-contributors}

Where each public name is defined, and the rules for moving one, are in
[API owners](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd):

- []{#migration-rules}[the rules for moving a public name](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#migration-rules);
- []{#geometry-api}[geometry names, from `scgsim.sgb` to `scgsim.geometry`](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#geometry-api);
- []{#aedt-api-transaction-and-state-ownership}[AEDT names and module owners](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#aedt-api-transaction-and-state-ownership);
- []{#palace-package-symbols}[Palace names](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#palace-package-symbols) and []{#palace-direct-submodule-exports}[Palace submodules](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#palace-direct-submodule-exports);
- []{#visualization-symbols}[visualization names](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#visualization-symbols) and []{#shared-presentation}[shared presentation](../contribute/internals/api-owners.qmd#shared-presentation);
